comment: Expected failures caused by the Java SDK (programs/java): the Java client (when.client java) and the Java agent (when.agent java). Each entry names the Phase B item that closes it; that item's commit deletes its entries. Client entries come first, so in a Java<->Java cell the client's (more specific) contains wins.

expectations.reason: The Java client has no $/cancel_request send
The Java client does not honour $/cancel_request from the agent; its fs read is never cancelled
The Java client has no $/cancel_request send
AcpAsyncClient has no generic request send
AcpAsyncClient has no generic notification send
The Java agent ignores $/cancel_request: the #slow prompt runs its full 10 s and answers end_turn
The Java agent cannot send $/cancel_request; it answers #fs read-slow with the chunk "cancel-request unsupported (P2)"
The Java agent has no generic request send; it answers #ext request with the chunk "ext: unsupported (P9)"
The Java agent has no generic request send
The Java agent has no generic notification send
The Java agent cannot register an extension request handler; it answers -32601
The Java agent cannot register an extension notification handler, so #ext last-notification answers "ext last: none"
The Java client does not honour the agent's $/cancel_request, so the fs read never ends with -32800

Java over HTTP: session/delete of an unknown id is posted session-scoped (inferred route, StreamableHttpRoutes.java:117-124) with Acp-Session-Id no-such-session, and the Java server answers 404 (StreamableHttpSessions.admitInbound); the RFD names no scope for session/delete and its POST tree has no 404 for an unknown session
